utility.notes: West Sacramento is in Yolo County; a 2006 ballot proposal to extend SMUD's public-utility service territory to include the Yolo County cities of West Sacramento, Davis, and Woodland was voted down, confirming PG&E has remained the electric utility for these cities since.

value.name: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E)
value.notes: Directly re-verified this session via Valley Clean Energy's own homepage, which explicitly names its service area as 'Davis, Woodland, Winters, and unincorporated Yolo County' -- West Sacramento is not among them. West Sacramento is also reportedly exploring joining Pioneer Community Energy per local news reporting, but has not joined as of this session (Pioneer's own current service-area page names only Placer/El Dorado County communities, not West Sacramento). PG&E is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

permit_authority.value: City of West Sacramento Building Division
permit_authority.notes: cityofwestsacramento.org returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session (both the dedicated SolarAPP+ page and the general Building Division page). This department name and page title are confirmed via search-engine indexing, but the page's specific content (eligibility, fees, timeline) could not be independently verified.

permit_url.notes: URL identified via search-engine indexing; cityofwestsacramento.org returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session, so its content could not be independently read or verified.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other PG&E-territory records in this dataset.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes West Sacramento/Yolo County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other PG&E-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

eligibility_constraints.notes: Search-engine summaries indicate the city uses SolarAPP+ (adopted September 2023) and classifies residential PV installs as 'Residential General,' with electronic plan submittal required since June 2022, but no size-cap or property-type figure could be independently confirmed via direct fetch this session.
